issues.reason: Core patterns' 'point at the words that put the atom there' test fails for (Member strasbourg city) — no kind word accompanies the name, and Names and casing licenses a type atom only when the sentence supplies the kind — so it asserts more than the text states.
(Member france country) is the same unlicensed world-knowledge typing; the text supplies only the name 'France'.

Categorical statements states outright that a property of a plural's members is never predicated of the group symbol — a bare (Member <group> <prop>) is for a property of the collection itself (size, name) — so (Member sk_producers_1 leading) is exactly the group-as-object reading the plural rules warn against.

gaps_confirmed: a predicative partitive 'X is one of the Ns' — Partitives quantifies a subset that then carries the predicate, and has no shape for a copular clause whose whole content is the subject's membership in a definite set
new_gaps: a comma-apposed place stack ('based in Strasbourg, France') — the containment rule is written for a second 'in <Place>' PP, so nothing states that the apposed larger place asserts (LocatedIn city country)

'based in' as a participial locative — the stative-locative route names 'is located in / is situated in' and the postural verbs, while the reduced-relative rule would instead demand an event, so the two routes are unresolved for this participle
repair_summary: Dropped (Member strasbourg city) and (Member france country), the two unstated world-knowledge typings — the names alone remain, as with 'Oslo' in the Time examples; replaced the group-level (Member sk_producers_1 leading) with the distributive rule (Implication (PartOf $x sk_producers_1) (Member $x leading)) at (STV 1.0 0.9), the form Quantifiers, generics & scope prescribes for a copular predicate over a definite group.
notes: Everything else is untouched, including the LocatedIn pair, the PartOf fallback for 'one of the …', the CardinalityPhrase with no invented number, and the group event plus per-member rule for the still-make relative clause.
